gpt-5.6-sol.m.bearer: A bearer is the physical optical wavelength (lambda) on a fiber span that carries one or more transport circuits—for example, 193.1 THz on the NY–FRA span carrying CIR-7. It is an internal transport-layer resource, not a client-facing service or any unrelated use of “bearer” or “wavelength.”
gpt-5.6-sol.m.circuit: A circuit is a provisioned end-to-end transport path through the optical core that underlays and carries a client-facing external service. It presents at hand-off points and is carried over one or more bearers; it is distinct from unrelated uses of “circuit” because it specifically denotes the managed transport construct, such as CIR-7 between New York and Frankfurt.
gpt-5.6-sol.m.grade: A **grade** classifies a circuit’s transport quality, specifically its physical protection and restoration level; examples include platinum, gold, and best-effort. It is an attribute of a circuit—not a general score, rank, or service grade—and indicates how resilient the circuit is to failures, such as whether it has dual-path protection.
gpt-5.6-sol.m.handoff: A hand-off is the physical demarcation point where a circuit terminates or is presented to the client’s equipment, such as the port where CIR-7 connects to a customer router. It is tied to a specific circuit and location, and is distinct from other uses of “handoff” that describe an operational transfer, workflow step, or change of responsibility rather than a physical network boundary.
gpt-5.6-sol.m.latency: Latency denotes the measured one-way propagation delay of a circuit path, expressed in milliseconds and primarily determined by path length—for example, 7.2 ms on CIR-7’s primary path. It is a property of the circuit and should be distinguished from round-trip time, processing or queuing delay, and unrelated metrics that also use the name “latency.”
gpt-5.6-sol.m.protection: Protection is a circuit-level resilience arrangement that preserves service during transport-path failures, such as a fiber cut or bearer loss, by switching traffic to a diverse path. It belongs to a specific circuit and includes schemes such as 1+1 path protection; it is distinct from unrelated uses of “protection,” such as access control, equipment safeguards, or data security.
gpt-5.6-sol.m.rate: In Meridian, **rate** is the committed end-to-end client payload throughput guaranteed for a circuit, such as 5 Gbit/s committed on CIR-7. It belongs to the circuit and is distinct from the underlying bearer’s physical line rate or raw interface speed.
